answer: A trellis of mutual attestation makes fake identities expensive: each newcomer must earn endorsements from established peers who stake their own reputation, and one bad endorsement sends a ripple of lost trust through the whole network, so a Sybil farmer would need to corrupt many independent reviewers at once. An opal-like reputation score, built slowly from verified work checked by randomly assigned peers, cannot be bought in bulk — each identity pays in time and real output before it can transact, while throwaway accounts stay at the bottom with no weight.
